title: Environmental assessment of daily mobility for the design of neighbourhoods: Coupling mobility microsimulation and life-cycle assessment
abstract: This paper aims to develop an environmental assessment methodology of daily mobility for neighbourhoods. Thus, a microsimulation model represents mobility at an individual scale, which is coupled with a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) for private cars and public transport to provide a holistic environmental assessment. The model is calibrated using census data and regional mobility surveys, providing information on population, jobs, dwellings, mobility and car fleets. The methodology is applied to a real neighbourhood project in Paris suburbs. Aggregated results show low environmental impacts of mobility compared to previous studies, with 276 kg CO2-eq per individual per year, reflecting the selected central and accessible location. Leveraging the microsimulation approach, disaggregated results highlight strong heterogeneity within both residents and employees, with respectively 17 % and 5 % of each group being responsible for half the emissions. Microsimulation further allows for estimating the effect of various levers to improve the project design. Although location exerts the greatest influence on the environmental impacts of mobility, reducing parking availability also proves very efficient, especially for residents. These findings support the use of microsimulation – instead of common mean approaches – to capture the heterogeneity of mobility behaviours and better estimate responses to levers in neighbourhood design.
abstractZh: 本文旨在建立街区日常移动的环境评估方法。研究通过微观模拟模型刻画个体尺度移动，并与私人汽车和公共交通的生命周期评价（LCA）耦合，实现综合环境评价。模型采用人口普查和区域出行调查数据校准，涵盖人口、就业、住房、移动和汽车车队等信息。该方法应用于巴黎郊区一个真实街区项目。聚合结果表明，相较既有研究，该项目的移动环境影响较低，人均每年为276千克二氧化碳当量，反映了其所处位置较为中心且可达性良好。微观模拟的分解结果揭示，居民与雇员内部均存在显著异质性：分别有17%的居民和5%的雇员贡献各自群体一半的排放。微观模拟还可估计不同调控手段对项目设计改进的影响。虽然区位对移动环境影响的作用最大，减少停车供给也十分有效，尤其适用于居民。研究支持采用微观模拟而非常见平均值方法，以刻画移动行为异质性，更准确估计人们对街区设计调控措施的响应。
